title: 📚 Future Participle (तव्य / अनीय)
description: Learn to use future participles to express obligation or necessity.

sections.title: 📖 What is the Future Participle?
sections.content: Future participles express obligation, necessity, or possibility. They are often translated as 'to be done' or 'should be done'.

formation.rule: Add 'तव्य' (tavya) or 'अनीय' (anīya) to the verb root.

examples.participle: गन्तव्यम् (gantavyam) - to be gone / should be gone
examples.sentence: गन्तव्यम् अस्ति। (It should be gone / It must be gone.)
पठितव्यं पुस्तकम्। (The book to be read.)
कर्तव्यं कार्यम्। (The work to be done.)
द्रष्टव्यं चित्रम्। (The picture to be seen.)

usage.example: कार्यं कर्तव्यम्। (The work must be done.)
गन्तव्यं भवति। (It can be gone / It is possible to go.)
त्वया पुस्तकं पठितव्यम्। (You should read the book.)

questions.question: What does 'कर्तव्यम्' mean?
questions.explanation: 'कर्तव्यम्' (kartavyam) means 'to be done / should be done'.

questions.question: How do you say 'to be read' in Sanskrit?
Translate: 'कार्यं कर्तव्यम् अस्ति।'
questions.explanation: 'कार्यं कर्तव्यम् अस्ति।' means 'The work must be done.'
